problem: Prior surveys cover only one or two of vision, language and robotics, and mostly describe architectures rather than the high-level challenges of embodied vision-language tasks. There is no holistic treatment that unifies navigation and manipulation tasks that use vision and language.
motivation: Embodied agents are expected to work alongside humans in physical environments, but current tasks, datasets and metrics mostly measure in-domain simulated success. The paper surveys the field to identify what blocks generalisation and real-world deployment.
key_idea: Define Embodied Vision-Language Planning (EVLP) as a task family with a unifying taxonomy (tasks, approaches, evaluation), then use it to derive core open challenges toward generalisable, real-world-deployable agents.
insight: The paper is a position/survey piece with no experiments or ablations. Its main message is that progress is limited by task and benchmark design (simulator realness, dataset realness, generalisation tests) and by the lack of principled domain knowledge such as pre-training and commonsense, rather than by architecture alone.
method: Problem definition: formalises EVLP as a planning problem Φ={S,A,s_ini,s_goal} with states built from the vision-language history; the agent minimises the difference between the admissible and predicted action sequences.

Task taxonomy: groups tasks into Vision-Language Navigation, Embodied Question Answering, Embodied Object Referral, Vision-and-Dialogue Navigation and Embodied Goal-directed Manipulation, distinguished by action space, reasoning mode and interaction.

Approaches taxonomy: covers supervised, reinforcement and hybrid learning; vision, language and planning architectures; and common techniques (data augmentation, multitask learning, pre-training, reward shaping).

Evaluation taxonomy: metrics grouped into distance, success, path similarity, instruction-based and object-centric; plus datasets and simulators compared along visual, language and demonstration dimensions.

Core challenges: new directions (social/dialogue interaction, dynamic environments, cross-task robot learning, interactive object perception), domain knowledge use, training objectives, and the simulation-to-real gap.
numbers_note: Survey extended abstract; no experimental results.
results: No empirical results. The contributions are a formal EVLP definition, a three-branch taxonomy, and a list of core challenges: generalisation, principled domain knowledge, training objectives and the sim-to-real gap.
limitations: Extended abstract with little detail; the full analysis is in the JAIR journal article.
No quantitative comparison of methods and no experiments to support the recommended directions.
